subject: Session flooring & bucketization — clarifying token accounting and packaging options
messages:
From: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@acme.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify billing model for our chat sessions (minimums / context / rounding)

Diego —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're excited by the latency and deterministic behavior your runtime showed. Before we scope an initial pilot I need clarity on how Redwood bills for the kinds of sessions our product will create so we can model TCO. A few concrete questions: 

- If a single chat request has a 1,200-token context (system + history) and the model emits 60 tokens, how do you bucket/round that? Do you bill input+output separately, or some combined quantum?
- Do you apply a per-request minimum (e.g., minimum billable chunk) or a monthly minimum per project?
- If we send the same system prompt for many sessions (session template), can that prompt be cached so we don't pay for it each request?
- Any special rules for streaming responses where tokens are emitted in smaller chunks?

We expect a steady stream of ~20k sessions/day initially, average generated tokens ~90, average context tokens 850. We are evaluating a committed contract if you can give us predictable billing with a modest discount — please propose packaging ideas as well.

Appreciate a concrete worked example (numbers) so we can plug into our model.

—Sam
Product Lead, Acme AI
Attachment: --none--
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@acme.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 11:32:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify billing model for our chat sessions (minimums / context / rounding)

Sam —

Great questions. I'll keep the answer concrete and include a worked example for the numbers you gave. TL;DR: Redwood bills per-token, but we use a per-call bucket called a "call unit" (explained below) and we support context caching for session templates which reduces repeat charges. We can build a committed package with a monthly minimum and tiered discounts — I attached a sketch proposal. 

How call units work (short):
- Count: we count input tokens and output tokens separately but charge the higher of the two in "call units" for each API call. This avoids double-billing tiny outputs in very large contexts.
- Quantum: call units are rounded up to the next 32-token bucket. So a 1 call unit = up to 32 tokens billed.
- Example math: if input=1,200 tokens and output=60 tokens, we compare (1,200) vs (60) -> bill the larger (1,200) as the basis. 1,200 / 32 = 37.5 -> round up to 38 buckets -> 38 call units. If your contract price = $0.0008 per call unit, that call costs 38 * $0.0008 = $0.0304.

Context caching (session templates):
- If you register a session template (system prompt + static prefix) and enable server-side prefix caching, the cached prefix is only billed the first time it is materialized per unique session key for the duration of the cache TTL. Subsequent calls that reuse the same cached prefix are billed only for the non-cached portion + generated output basis (still compared per-call). Practically: for repeated sessions with identical system prompt, you avoid paying the full input token charge every time.

Streaming behavior:
- Streaming tokens are aggregated per call and bucketed at the end; we do not apply an additional streaming penalty. The total emitted tokens are included in the output side of the call-unit comparison.

Worked example using your numbers (20k sessions/day, average context=850, gen=90):
- Per-call basis: compare input 850 vs output 90 -> bill 850 tokens -> 850/32 = 26.5625 -> round up -> 27 call units per call.
- If call unit price = $0.0008 -> per-call = 27 * $0.0008 = $0.0216
- Daily cost at 20k sessions = 20,000 * $0.0216 = $432.00/day -> ~ $12,960/month (30d)

Packaging / discounts we can offer:
- Option A (commit): 1M call units/month committed at 20% discount vs pay-as-you-go, overage billed at discounted rate.
- Option B (reserved + burst): 500k reserved call units + 50% burst capacity at normal committed price; useful if you expect growth variability.
- Option C (meter + cache optimization): no minimum but we provide a one-time configuration engagement to register session templates and caching rules; if caching reduces billable input tokens > 25% in the first 30 days, we apply a retroactive credit.

I've attached a short PDF proposal and a CSV with per-call examples so your finance model can run numbers. If you'd like, I can prepare a formal quote that converts call units into token-based estimates at the model(s) you plan to run.

Attachment: proposal-acme-commit-2028.pdf (PDF, 52KB)
Attachment: token-examples.csv (CSV, 6KB)

Next steps: if Option A looks reasonable I can put together a draft quote/term sheet and loop in finance/legal. Happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow to walk through the math.

—Diego
